Udhampur News: ग्रामीणों ने किया प्रदर्शन, रास्ता बहाल करने की मांग
विज्ञापन
उधमपुर। पंचायत हरतयान के वार्ड-2 (लरदागा लेहड़ी) में भूस्खलन के कारण रास्ता पूरी तरह से बदहाल हो गया है। सड़क सुविधा न होने और आवाजाही ठप पड़ने से उग्र हुए ग्रामीणों ने सोमवार को प्रशासन के खिलाफ जोरदार प्रदर्शन किया। प्रदर्शनकारियों ने जल्द से जल्द रास्ता बहाल करने और पहाड़ी धंसने से खतरे में आए मकानों को बचाने के लिए सुरक्षा (क्रेट) कार्य कराने की मांग की है। ग्रामीणों ने चेतावनी दी है कि यदि समस्या का तत्काल समाधान नहीं हुआ तो वे बड़ा आंदोलन शुरू करेंगे।
स्थानीय निवासी रवि कुमार व अन्य ग्रामीणों ने बताया कि इस रास्ते से करीब 250 परिवारों का रोजाना संपर्क जुड़ा हुआ है। लंबे समय से सड़क न बनने और हालिया भूस्खलन के बाद स्थिति जानलेवा हो चुकी है। पहाड़ी का बड़ा हिस्सा धंसने से कई मकानों की नींव हिल गई है, जिससे हादसे का डर बना हुआ है। रास्ते की खस्ताहाली का सबसे बुरा असर स्कूली बच्चों और बुजुर्गों पर पड़ रहा है। बच्चे रोजाना समय पर स्कूल नहीं पहुंच पा रहे हैं।

articles.title: Jammu Kashmir Consumers to Pay Rs 251 Crore More After Power Tariff Hike - Kashmir Life
articles.full_text:
SRINAGAR: Consumers in Jammu and Kashmir are expected to bear an additional financial burden of Rs 251 crore following a 6.83 per cent revision in electricity tariffs, the government informed the Legislative Assembly on Tuesday.
The tariff revision, notified by the Joint Electricity Regulatory Commission (JERC), is projected to generate an additional Rs 251 crore in revenue for the power distribution companies (DISCOMs) during 2026-27, the Power Development Department said in a written reply to a question by MLA Sajad Gani Lone.
The government said the revision was required to address the gap between the cost of supplying electricity and the revenue collected by the DISCOMs, as well as to meet their Annual Revenue Requirement (ARR).
Despite the increase, the government said it would provide more than Rs 4,500 crore in subsidy towards the DISCOMs’ power purchase costs.
The department further informed the House that Rs 4,385.30 crore in power tariff dues are outstanding against Jammu and Kashmir and Central Government departments.
Revenue collected from domestic consumers in the Kashmir Valley rose to Rs 1,455.90 crore in 2025-26 from Rs 1,238.07 crore in 2024-25, according to the government.
During the current financial year, domestic consumers had contributed Rs 547.79 crore in revenue up to August. Metered consumers accounted for Rs 383.08 crore, while Rs 164.71 crore was collected from flat-rate consumers.
The government also said the scheme offering 200 units of free electricity to eligible Antyodaya Anna Yojana (AAY) households is being implemented through a RESCO-based rooftop solar model under the PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana.
The tendering process for the scheme is currently under evaluation. The eligible households will begin receiving the benefit once the rooftop solar systems are commissioned.

articles.title: “Govt Failed to Give 200 Units Free Power, But Will Collect Rs 251 Cr More”: Sajad Lone - Kashmir Life
articles.full_text:
SRINAGAR: Peoples Conference president and Handwara MLA Sajad Gani Lone on Tuesday said the Jammu and Kashmir Government has acknowledged that the recent power tariff revision will result in an additional collection of Rs 251 crore from consumers.
Lone made the statement after the government responded to his question in the Legislative Assembly on the tariff revision and the installation of smart meters. His remarks were also posted on X.
According to Lone, the government has also informed the House that 11 lakh smart meters have been installed across Jammu and Kashmir since October 2024, when the present government took office.
Lone has repeatedly questioned the government over the National Conference’s pre-election promise to provide 200 units of free electricity to consumers in Jammu and Kashmir.
In its response in the Assembly on Tuesday, the government said the proposal to provide 200 units of free electricity was under examination.
The issue of free electricity and the impact of the revised tariff has been a recurring point of discussion between the government and opposition members in the Assembly, with Lone seeking clarification on the implementation of the electricity-related election commitment.
Lone said the government’s response on the additional revenue from the tariff revision and smart-meter installations had come in reply to his question.
